name: Euro-area economy
summary: Eurostat confirmed euro-area Q3 GDP growth of 0.4% on 13 Nov; October composite PMI 51.7, above 50
state: Eurostat's estimate of 13 Nov confirmed euro-area GDP growth of 0.4% in the third quarter, with employment stable (Eurostat). The final HCOB composite PMI for October fell to 51.7, a four-month low, but stayed above 50 (ActionForex). Both readings sit above the Normal lines; November flash PMIs are due later in the month.
for_you: Euro-area output is still growing, though momentum has slowed. Exporters and jobs tied to European demand are most exposed if the slowdown deepens.
rubric_hit: Normal: GDP +0.4% q/q (positive) and composite PMI 51.7 > 50

sources.title: GDP up by 0.4% and employment stable in the euro area - Euro indicators
Eurozone PMI Composite Falls to 51.7 as Demand Weakens and Business Confidence Slips

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
